2. `def-kleisli-category` — Definition

What is wrong: the [Definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-kleisli-category.md:27) says an arbitrary monad’s Kleisli category has “hom-sets.” The library instead calls arbitrary homs “hom-collections” and allows them to be proper classes ([category definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-category.md:45)); they are sets only under local smallness ([size definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-small-locally-small-and-large-category.md:32)).

Evidence: in the two-object proper-class-hom category above, with the identity monad,
\[
\mathcal C_T(0,1)=\mathcal C(0,1)=\{f_x:x\text{ is a set}\},
\]
a proper class. Thus the asserted “hom-set” is not a set. The construction remains valid if “hom-sets” is replaced by “hom-collections,” or if local smallness is assumed.

Severity: **fatal** — false size claim in the central Definition.

3. `rem-the-universal-properties-of-kleisli-and-eilenberg-moore-are-schematic` — second paragraph

What is wrong: the [Remark](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/rem-the-universal-properties-of-kleisli-and-eilenberg-moore-are-schematic.md:25) says \( [\mathcal C,\mathcal D] \) “is formed only under the hypotheses” of `prop-size-of-functor-categories`. That proposition only states sufficient conditions for local smallness or smallness:
> If \(\mathcal C\) is small and \(\mathcal D\) locally small, then the functor category is locally small; if both are small, it is small.

See the cited [proposition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/prop-size-of-functor-categories.md:26). The actual formation rule requires only that the source be small, without requiring the target to be locally small ([functor-category definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-functor-category.md:27)).

Evidence: take \(\mathcal C=\varnothing\) and let \(\mathcal D\) be the non-locally-small category above. The source is small, so the library forms \([\varnothing,\mathcal D]\); it is in fact the terminal category. Yet \(\mathcal D\) satisfies neither target-size hypothesis in the cited proposition.

Severity: **fatal** — a concrete false assertion and inaccurate characterization of the cited dependency in a `rem-` item, whose prose is its mathematical content.

## Focus checks that passed

The two uniqueness results establish strict uniqueness, not merely uniqueness up to natural isomorphism:

- For \(J\), \(JF_T=F\) fixes objects, and every Kleisli arrow decomposes using the Kleisli counit and \(F_T\); the counit equality therefore fixes \(J\) on every arrow.
- For \(K\), \(U^TK=U\) fixes underlying objects and arrows, while the Eilenberg–Moore counit equality fixes every algebra structure map.
- For \(M\), an arbitrary algebra homomorphism \(h:(TA,\mu_A)\to(TB,\mu_B)\) comes from \(h\eta_A\). The inverse calculation uses naturality and the monad laws, not monicity of \(\eta_A\). Fullness then makes the strict image the full subcategory on the literal free algebras.

The cited [Riehl](https://emilyriehl.github.io/files/context.pdf) and [Richter](https://www.math.uni-hamburg.de/en/personen/richter/bookdraft.pdf) treatments likewise use strict functors commuting with the left and right adjoints.
